```{r setup}
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Otani et al. (2025) characterised the population PK of mirikizumab, a
humanised IgG4 anti-IL-23p19 monoclonal antibody, in children and adolescents
(2 to <18 years, > 10 kg) with moderately to severely active ulcerative
colitis in the open-label phase II SHINE-1 study (NCT04004611). The adult
LUCENT 1+2 model (Chua 2023) was the starting point: a linear two-compartment
model with first-order absorption of subcutaneous (SC) doses. In the pediatric
fit the allometric exponents were fixed (0.8 on CL and Q, 1.0 on the volumes),
Ka and Q were fixed to the adult estimates, and time-varying albumin was the
only covariate retained besides weight.

The paper did not model exposure-response in children: the narrow exposure
range allowed only an exposure-quartile summary of the observed efficacy
endpoints (Figure 4) and an overlay on the adult AMAC exposure-response model
(Figure 5). The PK model is the only model in the paper.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Otani_2025_mirikizumab"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13286>

# Population

Baseline characteristics from Otani 2025 Table 1:

| Characteristic | 5 mg/kg IV (<= 40 kg) | 10 mg/kg IV (<= 40 kg) | 300 mg IV (> 40 kg) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N | 10 | 5 | 11 | 26 |
| Age, mean (SD), years | 9.6 (4.2) | 11.6 (1.1) | 14.0 (1.3) | 11.8 (3.4) |
| Male, % | 40.0 | 40.0 | 45.5 | 42.3 |
| White / Asian / Other, % | 50 / 40 / 10 | 60 / 40 / 0 | 90 / 10 / 0 | 68 / 28 / 4 |
| Weight, mean (SD), kg | 28.6 (9.0) | 33.0 (2.4) | 54.7 (13.3) | 40.5 (16.0) |
| Weight <= 20 kg, n | 2 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| BMI, mean (SD), kg/m^2 | 15.8 (2.3) | 17.0 (0.6) | 21.1 (5.0) | 18.3 (4.3) |

Induction was IV every 4 weeks (weeks 0, 4 and 8) by weight group: 300 mg
for > 40 kg, 5 or 10 mg/kg for > 20 to <= 40 kg, 5 mg/kg for <= 20 kg.
Maintenance was SC every 4 weeks from week 12 to week 48 by weight at week 12:
200 mg for > 40 kg, 100 mg for > 20 to <= 40 kg, 50 mg for <= 20 kg.
Week-12 non-responders received three more IV doses before maintenance. The
analysis used 232 serum samples; six troughs below the limit of
quantification were excluded (226 observations in the final fit). The same
information is in the model's `population` metadata.

# Source trace

The final estimates come from the NONMEM output in Appendix S1 (supplement 2),
which gives them to one more digit than Table 2. Rate constants and
clearances are published per hour and are multiplied by 24 to give the
per-day values used in the model file.

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment, first-order SC absorption, IV into central | ADVAN4 TRANS4 | Methods (Dose selection, Population PK analysis); Appendix S1 |
| Ka (1/h) | 0.00706, fixed | Appendix S1 THETA2; Table 2 footnote c |
| CL (L/h) | 0.0209 | Appendix S1 THETA3; Table 2 (0.021) |
| Vc = V2 (L) | 3.48 | Appendix S1 THETA4; Table 2 |
| Q (L/h) | 0.0087, fixed | Appendix S1 THETA5; Table 2 footnote c |
| Vp = V3 (L) | 1.40 | Appendix S1 THETA6; Table 2 |
| F1 | 0.498, estimated on the logit scale | Appendix S1 THETA1 and $PK; Table 2 footnote f |
| Weight on CL and Q | (WT/70.7)^0.8, fixed | Appendix S1 THETA9 and $PK; Table 2 footnote d |
| Weight on Vc and Vp | (WT/70.7)^1.0, fixed | Appendix S1 THETA10 and $PK; Table 2 footnote e |
| Albumin on CL | 1 + (-0.0218)(ALB - 45) | Appendix S1 THETA11 and $PK; Table 2 footnote d |
| IIV on CL (variance) | 0.128 (37.1%) | Appendix S1 OMEGA3; Table 2 |
| IIV on logit F1 (variance) | 0.471 (77.6%) | Appendix S1 OMEGA1; Table 2 |
| Proportional residual error | 0.288 (SIGMA fixed to 1) | Appendix S1 THETA7 and $ERROR |
| Additive residual error | 0, fixed (not carried) | Appendix S1 THETA8 |

Table 2 footnote b converts each variance as 100 sqrt(exp(OMEGA) - 1),
including the logit-scale variance of F1. The check below confirms that the
model-file variances reproduce the published percentages and the
weight-normalised summary values in the Results. The CL variance printed in
Appendix S1 (0.128) gives 37.0% rather than the 37.1% in Table 2 (which
would correspond to a variance of 0.129). The model uses the NONMEM output
value; the 0.1-point difference has no practical effect.

```{r source-check}
mod <- readModelDb("Otani_2025_mirikizumab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta
om <- ui$omega

iiv_pct <- c(
  CL = 100 * sqrt(exp(om["etalcl", "etalcl"]) - 1),
  F1 = 100 * sqrt(exp(om["etalogitfdepot", "etalogitfdepot"]) - 1)
)
cl_h <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) / 24
vss_per_kg <- (exp(th[["lvc"]]) + exp(th[["lvp"]])) / 70.7
f_pct <- 100 * plogis(th[["logitfdepot"]])

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tribble(
    ~Quantity, ~Model, ~Published,
    "IIV CL (%)", iiv_pct[["CL"]], 37.1,
    "IIV F1 (%)", iiv_pct[["F1"]], 77.6,
    "CL at 70.7 kg (L/h)", cl_h, 0.021,
    "Vss per kg at 70.7 kg (L/kg)", vss_per_kg, 0.069,
    "SC bioavailability (%)", f_pct, 49.8
  ),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Model values against Table 2 and the Results text."
)

# Closed-form: every quantity is computed from the model file alone and
# matches the published value to its printed precision.
stopifnot(
  abs(iiv_pct[["CL"]] - 37.1) < 0.3,
  abs(iiv_pct[["F1"]] - 77.6) < 0.15,
  round(cl_h, 3) == 0.021,
  round(vss_per_kg, 3) == 0.069,
  round(f_pct, 1) == 49.8
)
```

# Virtual cohort

Subject-level data are not public. Each SHINE-1 dose group gets 200 virtual
patients, with weights drawn from a normal distribution with the Table 1
mean and SD for that group, truncated to the group's weight band (which
raises the mean of the > 40 kg group by a few kilograms). Albumin
was not reported for the pediatric cohort and is held at the 45 g/L
reference value.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20250315)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20250315)

draw_weight <- function(n, mean, sd, lower, upper) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rnorm(4 * n, mean, sd)
    out <- c(out, x[x > lower & x <= upper])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

n_arm <- 200
groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~wt_mean, ~wt_sd, ~wt_lower, ~wt_upper,
  "> 40 kg: 300 mg IV", 54.7, 13.3, 40, 90,
  "<= 40 kg: 5 mg/kg IV", 28.6, 9.0, 12, 40,
  "<= 40 kg: 10 mg/kg IV", 33.0, 2.4, 20, 40
)

cohort <- groups |>
  mutate(arm = row_number()) |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(
    group = group,
    arm = arm,
    WT = draw_weight(n_arm, wt_mean, wt_sd, wt_lower, wt_upper)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    id = row_number(),
    ALB = 45,
    group = factor(group, levels = groups$group),
    iv_dose = case_when(
      arm == 1 ~ 300,
      arm == 2 ~ 5 * WT,
      arm == 3 ~ 10 * WT
    ),
    sc_dose = case_when(WT > 40 ~ 200, WT > 20 ~ 100, TRUE ~ 50)
  )

cohort |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_wt = mean(WT),
    sd_wt = sd(WT),
    min_wt = min(WT),
    max_wt = max(WT)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Dose group" = group,
    N = n,
    "Mean weight (kg)" = mean_wt,
    "SD weight (kg)" = sd_wt,
    "Min weight (kg)" = min_wt,
    "Max weight (kg)" = max_wt
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual SHINE-1 cohort.")
```

# SHINE-1 regimen over 52 weeks (Figure 2)

Each virtual patient receives three IV induction doses (weeks 0, 4 and 8,
40-minute infusions) followed by SC maintenance every 4 weeks from week 12
to week 48 at the dose for their weight. The figure shows the median and 90%
prediction interval of the simulated concentrations, the quantities whose
observed counterparts the prediction-corrected VPC in Figure 2 of Otani 2025
compares.

```{r regimen}
inf_dur <- 40 / 1440

regimen_events <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = c(0, 28, 56)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = iv_dose, rate = iv_dose / inf_dur, cmt = "central"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = seq(84, 336, by = 28)) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = sc_dose, rate = 0, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = seq(0, 364, by = 1)) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, WT, ALB, group) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_regimen <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = regimen_events,
  keep = "group",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r fig2, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.5}
sim_regimen |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    q50 = median(Cc),
    q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, q50, colour = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 52, by = 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)",
    y = "Mirikizumab concentration (ug/mL)",
    colour = "Induction group", fill = "Induction group",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated SHINE-1 regimen (median and 90% PI);",
      "compare with Figure 2 of Otani 2025."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Steady-state exposure by dose group (Figure 3)

Figure 3 of Otani 2025 shows the model-estimated steady-state Cmax, AUC over
the 4-week dosing interval and Cavg for each pediatric weight and dose group.
Steady state is reached here with explicit dose trains: six IV doses every 4
weeks for induction, and ten SC doses every 4 weeks for maintenance. NCA is
taken over the last interval of each. Maintenance groups are defined by
weight band, as in the figure: > 40 kg receiving 200 mg and > 20 to <= 40 kg
receiving 100 mg. The same patients are re-used, so the maintenance groups
pool the induction arms by weight.

```{r ss-events}
iv_ss <- tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, dose_no = 0:5) |>
  mutate(
    time = 28 * dose_no,
    evid = 1L,
    amt = iv_dose,
    rate = iv_dose / inf_dur,
    cmt = "central",
    treatment = paste("Induction:", group)
  )
iv_obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(
  cohort,
  time = c(0, seq(140, 168, by = 0.25), 140 + inf_dur)
) |>
  mutate(
    evid = 0L,
    amt = 0,
    rate = 0,
    cmt = "central",
    treatment = paste("Induction:", group)
  )

sc_cohort <- cohort |>
  filter(WT > 20) |>
  mutate(
    id = id + nrow(cohort),
    treatment = ifelse(
      WT > 40,
      "Maintenance: > 40 kg: 200 mg SC",
      "Maintenance: > 20 to <= 40 kg: 100 mg SC"
    )
  )
sc_ss <- tidyr::expand_grid(sc_cohort, dose_no = 0:9) |>
  mutate(time = 28 * dose_no, evid = 1L, amt = sc_dose, rate = 0, cmt = "depot")
sc_obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(sc_cohort, time = c(0, seq(252, 280, by = 0.25))) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, cmt = "central")

ss_events <- bind_rows(iv_ss, iv_obs, sc_ss, sc_obs) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, rate, cmt, WT, ALB, treatment) |>
  distinct(id, time, evid, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = ss_events,
  keep = "treatment",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r nca}
sim_nca <- sim_ss |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_nca <- ss_events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = sort(unique(sim_nca$treatment)),
  cmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  cav = TRUE
) |>
  mutate(
    start = ifelse(grepl("^Induction", treatment), 140, 252),
    end = start + 28
  )

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(
  PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals)
)
```

## Comparison against Figure 3

The reference values are the box-plot medians of Figure 3, read from the
figure by the maintainers; reading error is a few percent. Figure 3 summarises
the individual estimates of the 26 participants (2 to 11 per group), so each
reference median is itself uncertain.

```{r nca-compare}
fig3_medians <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast, ~cav,
  "Induction: > 40 kg: 300 mg IV", 122, 700, 25.5,
  "Induction: <= 40 kg: 5 mg/kg IV", 107, 520, 19,
  "Induction: <= 40 kg: 10 mg/kg IV", 212, 1560, 56,
  "Maintenance: > 40 kg: 200 mg SC", 15, 230, 8.2,
  "Maintenance: > 20 to <= 40 kg: 100 mg SC", 12.5, 225, 8.0
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = fig3_medians,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "day*ug/mL", cav = "ug/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated steady-state medians vs Figure 3. * differs from the figure by >20%."
)
```

```{r nca-assert}
cav_med <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(fig3_medians, treatment, fig = cav), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - fig) / fig)

# Centre of the distribution for the three groups with 8 to 11 participants
# behind the figure median: a wrong clearance, bioavailability, allometric
# exponent or unit conversion moves Cavg by far more than 25%.
cav_large <- cav_med |> filter(!grepl("10 mg/kg", treatment))
stopifnot(all(abs(cav_large$pct_diff) < 25))

# Results text: exposure at 10 mg/kg was about 2-fold the 5 mg/kg exposure.
ratio_10_5 <- cav_med$sim[grepl("10 mg/kg", cav_med$treatment)] /
  cav_med$sim[grepl("5 mg/kg", cav_med$treatment)]
round(ratio_10_5, 2)
stopifnot(ratio_10_5 > 1.7, ratio_10_5 < 2.6)
```

Every simulated median is within 20% of the figure except the Cavg of the
10 mg/kg group (5 participants), which sits above the simulation in the
figure: the model gives a typical Cavg of about 43 ug/mL for a 33 kg
child at 10 mg/kg, while the figure median is about 56 ug/mL. The figure
reflects the post hoc clearances of those five children, and the Results
describe the 10 mg/kg exposure only as about 2-fold the 5 mg/kg exposure,
which the model reproduces.

# Individual SC bioavailability

Table 2 footnote f reports the geometric mean (CV%) of the individual post
hoc bioavailabilities in SHINE-1 as 47.5% (27.9%). Post hoc estimates are
shrunk toward the typical value (eta shrinkage on F1 was 24% in Appendix S1),
so the simulated distribution, which uses the full estimated variance, is
wider.

```{r bioavailability}
f_sim <- sim_regimen |> distinct(id, fdepot)
tibble(
  "Simulated median F (%)" = 100 * median(f_sim$fdepot),
  "Simulated geometric mean F (%)" = 100 * exp(mean(log(f_sim$fdepot))),
  "Simulated geometric CV (%)" = 100 * sqrt(exp(var(log(f_sim$fdepot))) - 1),
  "Post hoc geometric mean F (%)" = 47.5,
  "Post hoc geometric CV (%)" = 27.9
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Individual SC bioavailability.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Albumin.** The pediatric albumin distribution is not reported. The
  simulations hold albumin at the 45 g/L reference, where the albumin
  multiplier on CL is 1. Children with lower albumin have higher clearance
  (about 11% higher at 40 g/L).
- **Weight as a time-fixed covariate.** Table 2 labels the weight effect
  "baseline weight"; the control stream reads it from a column named BWTV.
  The simulations hold weight constant, which makes the distinction moot
  here. Users simulating growth over long periods may supply time-varying
  weight.
- **Additive residual error.** The control stream fixes the additive
  component to 0, so the model carries a proportional error only.
- **Fixed parameters.** Ka, Q and both allometric exponents were fixed in
  the paper and are wrapped in `fixed()`. The IIV on Ka, Vc, Q and Vp was
  fixed to 0 in the control stream and is not carried.
- **IV infusion duration.** The Methods give "at least 40 minutes"; the
  simulations use 40 minutes.
- **Steady state.** Figure 3 reports steady-state exposures without stating
  how they were computed. The simulations use explicit dose trains (six IV
  doses, ten SC doses) and take the last interval.
- **Combined adult-pediatric model.** The Discussion mentions a fit to
  pooled adult and pediatric data with estimated allometric exponents (0.607
  on CL and Q, 0.58 on the volumes), but reports no other parameters for it,
  so it is not provided.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weights are drawn from truncated normal distributions
  matching the Table 1 means and SDs; the paper used the observed
  participants.

# Reference

* `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Otani_2025_mirikizumab"))$reference`
